Measures whole body insulin action, and the ability of insulin to stimulate glucose uptake into specific peripheral tissues, whiles also assessing the suppression of glucose production. In this assay, Insulin concentrations are acutely raised and then subsequently maintained by a continuous infusion of insulin. Plasma glucose levels are held contant at a basal level through infusion of glucose (euglycemia). Once steady-state is reached, the glucose infusion rate will equal glucose uptake by all the peripheral tissues, and be analyzed as a measure of how sensitive beta cells in a specific system are to insulin action.

Measures the breakdown of triglycerides into free fatty acids (FFAs), in isolated adipocytes and in the serum of mice stimulated/treated by catecholamines such as, noradrenaline and adrenaline, or B-adrenergic agonist such as, isoproterenol.

Non-esterified fatty acids (NEFAs) are primarily derived from the hydrolysis of triglycerides in the adipose tissue by hormone-sensisitive lipase (HSL). NEFAs in each sample is converted to Acetyl-CoA, AMP, and pyrophosphoric acid (PPi) via Acetyl-COA synthetase (ACS). Acetyl-CoA is oxidized to form 2,3-trans-Enoyl-CoA and hysrogen peroxide via enzyme Acetyl-CoA oxidase (ACOD). The hydrogen peroxide reacts with peroxidase to produce a blue purple pigment via oxidation condensation with 3-Methyl-N-Ethyl-N-(B-Hydroxyethyl)-Aniline (MEHA) and 4-amino-antipyrine (4-AA).
Hemolymph extracted from adult flies. DAGs separated from other lipid classes by TLC and quantified by densitometry.
B-hydroxybutryate (ketone) production is measured in serum and metabolic tissue homogenates (liver; kidneys).

Assay utilizes hydrolysis reaction of triglycerides found in sample by lipase into glycerol and FFAs. Glycerol is then phosphorylated by ATP via Glycerol kinase (GK) to produce Glycerol-3-phosphate which is oxidized via dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DAP) and hydrogen peroxide. 4-aminoantipyrine (4-AAP) and 3,5-dichloro-2-hydroxybenzene sulfonate (DHBS) reacts with sample to produce a red-colored pigment measured via absorbance between 500 - 550 nm.

Mass spectometry-based imaging technique in which pre-frozen, thin liver sections, are processed within a matrix using analyte (lipid) specific specific solvents, capable of absorbing laser wavelengths for subsequent analyte ionization which can be visualized and spatially mapped.

Mass spectometry-based imaging technique in which an electrically charged solvent is sprayed onto the freshly frozen, or FFPE embedded tissue sections, desorbing, and ionizing analytes (lipids) which are then detected and visualized.

Mass spectometry-based imaging technique in which ions on a sample surface are accelerated by a primary ion beam. Incorporating the time it takes heavy vs lighter ions across a sample, to reach the detector, lipids within samples can be identified by differences in mass and spatially mapped with sub-micrometer resolution.
